newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes puts gold reserves at 3.02 mln oz.
newsitem.headline: Macraes puts gold reserves at 3.02 mln oz.

text.p: Macraes Mining Company on Thursday reported a sharp increase in gold reserves to 3.02 million ounces following a successful drilling programme.
Macraes reported proved and probable ore reserves at 59.5 million tonnes grading 1.58 grams/tonne, representing a total of 3.02 million ounces of gold.
Macraes Chairman Brettney Fogarty told Reuters the figures, released in its company's September quarterly report, referred only to the Macraes project near Dunedin, New Zealand.
The estimate of reserves was up by 1.4 million ounces or 78 percent since the previous estimate a year ago.

The total mineral resource at June 30 stood at 89.8 million tonnes averaging 1.5 g/tonne, representing 4.33 million ounces. Reserves are defined as the portion of resources that can economically be extracted.
Fogarty said Macraes, historically, had been able to extract 55 percent of resources economically. "This estimate says that we can now extract 70 percent."
He said the increase had been brought about by lower unit operating costs and production and geological efficiencies.
Macraes has drilled 182,800 metres at the project in the two and a half years to June 30, and plans to drill another 600,000 metres in the three years from January 1, 1997.

As previously announced, the expanded operation will employ 500 people when complete and treble ore throughput to nine million tonnes a year. Gold production is forecast to rise to 320,000-350,000 ounces a year from 120,000.
